status: G4 rest: processed, compressed and reviewed; ships as g4-donkey, in Chapters VI, IX, XI and XII (on the web in Chapter XI only)
use: A pack donkey with panniers of pots beside the pottery stall in the courts beyond the board (Chapters VI, IX, XI and XII).

generator.prompt: A Roman pack donkey of the mid-3rd century AD standing square: all four legs straight and vertical, evenly spaced, head held level and facing forward, tail hanging straight down, symmetrical. A small sturdy donkey about 1.1 metres at the withers with a dusty grey coat, a dark cross over the shoulders, a pale muzzle and belly, long upright ears and a short upright dark mane, wearing a plain rope halter and a simple wooden pack saddle on a woollen pad, with a wicker pannier hanging on each side filled with clay jars packed in straw. Realistic proportions, anatomically accurate. Single isolated model with complete geometry from every side and a bold, solid, readable silhouette from above. No ground plane, no display plinth, no text or inscriptions, no modern objects, no fantasy elements.

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the camps in the desktop build at High
review.notes: As asked, though darker grey than dusty: long upright ears, a pale muzzle, a short dark mane and a halter, under a pale pack pad, with a wicker basket of clay jars at each side, 1.60 m long and 1.4 m to its ear tips. Beside Chapter XI's pottery stall its long ears and baskets of jars read at once; in Chapter IX its court lies 16 m beyond the board, so the camera must be drawn back to take it in, and there it is small.
